chunks: You will see the evil-doers full of fear of what they deserve, yet it will come to pass. But those who believe and do the right will be in gardens of Paradise. They will receive what they wish from their Lord; and this will be the greatest favour.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the fate of the unjust and the righteous in the Hereafter according to this verse?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shura, this verse serves as a concluding affirmation of divine justice, contrasting the psychological torment of the unjust with the serene abundance of the righteous. Shia exegetes, such as Allamah Tabatabai, highlight that 'what they wish for' signifies not merely material gratification but the ultimate spiritual satisfaction of beholding the Divine Countenance, representing the pinnacle of *Fadl* (divine grace).
